title: Classical Sufficiency in Quantum Statistical Experiments: the posterior covariance in the multinomial experiment (Lemma D.1)
author: Samriddha Lahiry
work: Classical Sufficiency in Quantum Statistical Experiments
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's posterior-covariance lemma for the multinomial experiment, printed as Lemma D.1 (source0.tex lines 6113-6168) and delivered with the paper's own complete 466-line proof (lines 6170-6635). The statement identifies the posterior distribution of the multinomial parameter given the counts, on the ordered simplex and under the paper's Dirichlet-type prior, and exhibits its covariance matrix in closed form, which is the tool the paper uses to compare the classical and quantum experiments. The proof is the paper's own long computation: it rewrites the posterior density in the ordered coordinates, identifies the normalising constant through the Dirichlet integral, computes every second moment by a change of variables to the simplex and repeated beta-integral evaluations, and assembles the covariance matrix entry by entry, with the symmetric statistics of the multinomial handled by an explicit combinatorial expansion. This is a research-level computation in quantum statistics rather than a qualifying-examination exercise, so the unit is H2. Delivered with the paper's own proof, in the paper's own notation, as the single primary proof body; the unit is H2.
